description: a 20-person brand agency in launch week for its biggest client

business.name: Halfmoon and Co
business.description: Halfmoon and Co is a twenty-person brand and film agency working with challenger sports and outdoor brands. Kestrel Athletic is forty percent of their revenue, the spring campaign goes live on Friday at 06:00 under press embargo, and the client has asked for a change to the hero film four days out with the colour grade already locked.

cast.name: Nadia Farrow
cast.voice: Calm, specific, allergic to vagueness. Restates what she has just been told in one sentence to check it, then names the decision and the owner.

cast.name: Theo Lindqvist
cast.voice: Writes in fragments and images, no capital letters in Slack, and takes any note on the work personally for about ninety minutes before agreeing with it.

cast.name: Bea Ofori
cast.voice: Diplomatic to a fault. Every email has a warm opener, a soft ask and a hard deadline hidden in the last line. Copies people in early.

cast.name: Jonah Weiss
cast.voice: Cheerful, over-promises on turnaround, then works until 3am to make it true. Sends render links with no context and one emoji.

cast.name: Lucia Marrone
cast.voice: Schedules and money. Writes numbered lists, chases twice and then escalates without drama. Never uses an exclamation mark.

cast.name: Clive Barrow
cast.voice: Friendly and completely immovable. Frames every late change as a small favour, uses 'quick' about things that take two days, and cc's his CMO when he means it.

cast.name: Moira Deng
cast.voice: Terse, deadline-driven, everything in bold-sounding capitals about embargo times. Assumes you have read the last three emails.

threads.subject: Hero film - one small change before Friday

messages.body:
Nadia,

We showed the cut internally this morning and it went down very well. One small thing: our CMO would like the new logo lockup at the end rather than the one in the cut, and ideally the last line of VO changed from 'built for the long way round' to 'made for the long way round'.

I know it is late. Should be quick? We are still good for Friday 06:00.

Clive

Clive — to be clear on what that is: the lockup swap re-opens the grade on the last eleven seconds, and a VO change is a re-record with Ilse plus a new mix. That is two days, not two hours, and delivery to the platforms is Thursday 18:00.

I can do one of the two by Friday. Which is it?

Nadia

Understood, and thank you for being straight with me. Let me come back to you after my 4pm — cc'ing our CMO so she has the context.

If it helps, the logo is the one she actually cares about.

Clive

threads.subject: EMBARGO — Friday 06:00 BST, assets to press list

messages.body:
Embargo lifts Friday 06:00 BST. Press list is 41 outlets, four have exclusives and one of those is print with a Wednesday night print deadline.

I need final stills and the 30 second cut in the press kit by Thursday 12:00 or the exclusives go without assets.

Moira

Nothing in the kit yet. Thursday 12:00 is tomorrow.

If the film is moving, tell me now — I can hold two of the four, I cannot hold print.

threads.subject: Freelance invoices - motion team, June and July

messages.body:
Nadia,

1. Three freelance motion invoices are sitting unapproved: 4,200, 2,800 and 6,150.
2. Two of them are now 45 days out and one of those people is Ilse, who we need on Thursday for a possible VO re-record.
3. I have chased twice.

Approve them and I will get them paid this week.

Lucia

the grade is locked and i would like it to stay locked. the last eleven seconds are the only part of this film anyone will remember and they took four days.

if the lockup changes we are not swapping a layer, we are re-lighting the end of the film. i will do it if we decide to do it, but nobody should say the word quick.

t
for what it's worth i can prep both versions overnight so we're not deciding under time pressure tomorrow. render farm is free after 20:00 :)

Jonah — yes, prep both, but do not start the re-grade until we have Clive's answer in writing. Theo, you are right and nobody is calling it quick.

Decision by 10:00 tomorrow at the latest, from me.

Nadia

notes.body: Wants the last eleven seconds of the hero film re-cut. Grade is locked, Jonah is on it either way. Bea asked twice whether this is a change order; Clive did not answer either time.

notes.body: Clive raised autumn himself at the end of the screening. Nothing in writing. Nadia's read: it is ours if Friday goes cleanly and gone if it does not.

tasks.content: Get the hero film change in writing as a change order
Pay the June and July motion invoices before Friday
Book the Rowan Outdoor call for next week

paragraphs.text: Everything that has to be in a platform's hands before Friday 06:00 BST.
Hero 60s — graded, locked, awaiting the re-cut of the last eleven seconds.
Cutdowns 30s / 15s / 6s — delivered, but they inherit the hero's tail, so all four move if the re-cut lands.
Press kit — with Moira. Embargoed copy still says TBC on the availability date.
Thursday 16:00 for broadcast, Thursday 22:00 for social. Nothing after that is our decision to make.
v7 — grade locked, signed off by Clive on the screening call.
v8 — requested Tuesday: replace the last eleven seconds with the alternate ending. Grade would have to re-open. Colourist is on another job until Thursday morning.
Theo's position: the alternate ending was cut for a reason and the reason has not changed.
Embargo: Friday 06:00 BST. Thirty-one outlets on the list, four of which have broken an embargo for this client before.
Assets go out Thursday morning with the embargo line in the subject and in the first paragraph of the body.
Availability date in the boilerplate is still TBC — Bea to confirm with Kestrel.
